problem: Embodied navigation agents depend on DNNs and LLMs that are vulnerable to attacks, yet safety work is scattered across attacks, defenses and benchmarks. No survey covers safety of embodied navigation in general; related surveys cover navigation without safety, or embodied-AI safety in healthcare only.
motivation: Embodied navigation is deployed in safety-critical settings such as robotics and autonomous driving. Physical perturbations (patches, light) and model-level attacks (jailbreak, backdoor) can make agents deviate, misidentify obstacles, or collide. A structured view of threats, mitigations and evaluation is needed to guide research.
key_idea: Provide the first systematic survey of embodied navigation safety, organized as attacks (physical vs model-based), defenses (physical vs model-based) and evaluation (datasets and metrics), plus future directions.
insight: The survey shows the field is immature. Physical defenses are few, and most defenses are borrowed from non-embodied tasks. Most work is qualitative or uses purpose-built datasets, so studies cannot be compared directly. LLM/multimodal attacks and verification (robustness thresholds, theoretical bounds) are largely unexplored.
method: Taxonomy: splits safety into attacks, defenses and evaluation, with attacks and defenses each divided into physical and model-based.
Physical attacks: reviews 2D patches, 3D patches/camouflage, multi-view patches (EOT-style) and adversarial light (laser, electromagnetic injection).
Model-based attacks: reviews RL-based attack optimization, federated-learning backdoors, LLM backdoors (word, scene, RAG triggers) and LLM jailbreaks (voice, suffix, targeted/untargeted).

Defenses: reviews physical defenses (patch detection/removal, certified small-receptive-field CNNs, Embodied Active Defense) and model-based defenses (Prompt-Based Aggregation for FL, Llama-Guard/HarmBench, prompt- and model-level jailbreak defenses).

Evaluation: compares datasets for classic models and for LLMs (e.g., GOAT-Bench, SafeAgentBench, EARBench, DivScene, LoTa-Bench), and metrics (human-based, formula-based SR/SPL/SEL/GC, model-based GPT-4 judging).
Future directions: attacks in dynamic environments, white-box and multimodal attacks; runtime-monitoring defenses; unified evaluation; verification techniques.
numbers_note: Survey paper; no experimental results reported.
results: Provides the first taxonomy of embodied navigation safety across attacks, defenses and evaluation, with tables of representative attacks, defenses and datasets. It identifies gaps: limited physical defenses, non-unified evaluation, and no verification frameworks.
limitations: Coverage of navigation-specific safety work is thin, and many cited works concern manipulation or driving rather than navigation.
Purely descriptive, with no quantitative comparison of methods, and defenses/evaluation are treated briefly.
Future directions are high-level, without concrete protocols.
compares_to: Vision-and-Language Navigation: Today and Tomorrow survey
Screens to Scenes (embodied AI in healthcare safety survey)
